body:
Nice, code looks good to me. It might need thorough testing to make sure everything works (especially all tiles editors).

For the ratio I think I would go with a value between 0.0 and 1.0, even if it's converted to 0.5 under the hood. I agree that "flat side length" might be a bit easier to understand (though, TBH, I think we could find something better)
Also, I think the a function to compute the overlap ratio could be added to TileSet. This code is used often so it might deserve a dedicated private function IMO.

I've examined the code some more and found that for configuration of **Hexagon Shape** and **0.5 tile offset** the grid is visually identical to **Isometric Shape**, however the behaviour for `get_neighbor_cell` function becomes different(isometric shape has 4 neighbors, when hexagons have 6). 
I believe, this is the only configuration which produces discrepancies. I don't think this is a deal breaker for this feature though, but I am unsure of the best way to go about fixing it right now.
This configuration(hexagon, 0.5 offset) should not be used by users any way as it is visually identical to isometric view(and just swapping it in the editor produces no visual discrepancy, which is good). There are a few ways I'm currently thinking of fixing it:
- Adding a warning when using an offset of 0.0 or 0.5. (sounds like the best option, will create a commit with this soon)
- Clamping the value. (Doesn't feel the best, the clamp amount would feel arbitrary)
- Forcefully switching to another shape when 0.0 or 0.5 overlap is reached. (Relatively fine in editor, absolute hell for programming api.) Somewhat better if swap happens at scene run time, but still quite bad.
- Accounting for this case in the backend code. (also fine, but will dirty up the code quite a bit, there are a lot of checks for Isometric shape as is, just more visual clutter will be added. Potentially a decently clean solution if a helper function is to be created, but then there will exist a weird helper function which people will need to remember to use when checking for the shape.)

If it was to me I would just leave it as a warning, since users have the shape of "hexagon" and it kind of implies the existence of 6 neighbors. Configurations with 0.0 and 0.5 are are also a bit less optimized since they use 6 vertices for a polygon instead of 4, while visually being rectangles. Need maintainers opinion I think.
Would be happy to receive feedback on what is the best way to go about this issue.

Sorry for not being able to express my thoughts more concisely.
Aaand apologies for not being as thorough as I should have been when first creating this PR.

Hmm, I think a warning could be fine, but I don't think we have warnings for resources configuration (they require a node). And I don't think we should delegate this warning to the TileMap node. If we find a way to do so, I'm ok with a warning.

Otherwise, I believe clamping the value could be fine. If we don't want to do it in the engine, we could do it editor-only. We could clamp between, let's say, 0.1 and 0.9, but allow other value with the "or_greater" and "or_lesser" property hints.

Refactored to have a function to get the overlap.
Decided to name the parameter "flat side ratio", its not perfect but I like the idea of the variable being from 0.0 to 1.0, and other explanations don't quite work with that, rate of wedging or interlocking is 0.0 to 0.5, "overlap" has to introduce invisible bounding boxes. I think my "flat side ratio" ends up being pretty clear.
Added an editor warning for when the value of 0.0 and 1.0 is reached <- this has to be double checked if editor warnings are fine to use that way, I think they are. Also an important note: the way I wrote the warning it will warn every time the scene is opened where tile_set with those values is used. Because it checks if the tile_shape is hexagon, it _will not_ throw a warning if a user edits the flat side ratio first and then changes the shape this can only be done via a script. It will also not warn if you change from a different shape to a hexagon when the flat side ratio is at 0.0 or 1.0 already(when it was first set the shape must have been hexagon, so the warning appeared at first setting of the parameter). I think these cases are fine because the warnings should catch regular use cases, and if they don't it will still warn on consequent file open.
sorry for being too wordy again

> Added an editor warning for when the value of 0.0 and 1.0 is reached <- this has to be double checked if editor warnings are fine to use that way, I think they are. Also an important note: the way I wrote the warning it will warn every time the scene is opened where tile_set with those values is used. Because it checks if the tile_shape is hexagon, it will not throw a warning if a user edits the flat side ratio first and then changes the shape this can only be done via a script. 

No I don't think it's fine. Either the value is fine and it should not print anything, or it's not and it should be disallowed. I think those warning can be removed if the editor slider cannot allow those values by default (see the suggestion below). 

That being said, I think the warning could be added to the documentation instead. Something like "Using 0.0 or 1.0 as a value is discouraged, use the corresponding tile shape instead."

Added the modifier variable as discussed.
However I have a few gripes with it
<details>
  <summary>Consider checking the version where I store the overlap float value.</summary>
   https://github.com/508312/godot/tree/overlap_float_stored_to_disk
   
 The original problems with precision happened because of editor rounding, not the variable itself being impercise.
  
  Modifier offset variable is a tad bit more precise, though(which was weird to me since there are about 10 times more floating point numbers between 0 and 0.5 than between 1 and 1024). Modifier offset can represent numbers to full accuracy when length is using a power of two as a fraction, so the step has to be that to take full advantage, i.e. 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, thats fine since a step of 0.5 allows the flat side to begin/end in 4 points for each pixel. If using arbitrary floats the two variables have the same issues. So modifier should be used if length step size isn't power of 2.
  
 That being said, I think the noticeable differences between modifier offset variable and just storing overlap value only happen by the time where default shapes, like half-offset square begin becoming inaccurate too. It happened at ~1000 tiles out, for 129px tiles. Square offset tiles start to show pixel inaccuracies at ~1300 tiles.
 
 So unless these levels of precision are required I would just go with storing overlap value directly.
 Some upsides of storing overlap:
-  It's always valid, setting the size to a huge number, then making flat side length near that huge number and scaling the size down won't result in a value which logically places flat side end outside of the tile. For the modifier offset clamping is required, because, if you set the size to huge value, the modifier is also huge, without clamping the shape of the hexagon wants to be in the range where the tile selection is broken, those values must not be possible through the editor, through the script is probably fine. You can't clamp length or modifier because they depend on size.
- You can remove the clamping. With storing overlap directly you can disallow or_less, or_greater in the editor, but still trust the programmer and allow unclamped overlap to be set via the script, since its not outright broken visually and produces either perspective effect, or effect of having gaps between tiles. (50/50 on this since well tile selection is not reliable in that case). The clamps aren't the best for compat in case higher range of overlap will be supported(which it probably wouldn't).
- Overlap preserves shape when changing tile size.

I don't know, the overlap is just nice to store since that's the actual math variable used.

Haven't tried switching modifier overlap to double, but if precision is the only issue, maybe thats the move(though I don't know, the .tres value saving might be the bottleneck).

I would compare the two versions and decide if the added precision is worth it. Again the modifier offset can be precise up to the point that shapes become imprecise, the overlap becomes a little bit more unstable a bit earlier, but to me not enough earlier to not be using it, I advocate for storing tile overlap on disk, its more universal.
</details>

After thinking about it, I decided to not go with storing modifier as an offset from tile_size/2. The precision is not a problem without the editor rounding. Exposed `flat_side_length` only in the editor as a proxy, not for scriping, because in the code order of operations between setting `tile_size` and `flat_side_length` would have mattered. Exposed the raw `hexagonal_tile_overlap` for the scripting api, mostly because majority of the use cases should be handled by modifying the `flat_side_length` in the editor. Just felt more right to expose the "real" underlying value (or rather the standard way to represent the overlap) in code, with the assumption that it is there for more complex use cases not covered by the editor. Though maybe I should add a helper method for conversions between overlap and length, lmk.

Should be relatively clean now. The only nitpick it that for hexagonal tiles only, dragging the `tile_size`(to change it) doesn't work. This doesn't feel the best but I don't think there is a way around this, if `flat_side_length` is to be dynamically updated. This behavior is also seen with the `Hframes` and `Vframes` inside of `Sprite2D`->animation, just as an example of this happening in other parts of the editor.
